environment.substrate: headless Chromium: real layout and hit-testing, a click is a mouse press at the element's box, typing is key events; virtual clock; one small fixed window

parameters.split_rule: sha256(task name) mod 4 == 0 is development, the rest held out

read_this_first: Run 3. Three things differ from V1 and V2 and none of the three numbers may be compared across them without saying so. (1) SUCCESS NOW MEANS THE PAGE'S FULL REWARD. V1 and V2 counted any positive reward; some pages pay part of the reward for part of the task, so V1 and V2 are too generous there (find-greatest, use-colorwheel and use-colorwheel-2 were counted as solved by replay and are not). (2) The pages run in headless Chromium with real mouse and key input, not in a headless DOM. (3) The first success is searched for in an order read off the instruction (--search guided); every action is still tried. NO TASK IS HELD OUT ANY MORE: the producer read per-task failures after V1, and wrote the guided order after reading pages and tried it on about 18 of these tasks. The names 'development' and 'held_out' below are the same hash split as in V1 and are kept only so that rows line up; here they do not mean unseen. Checked by the producer only: the 65 tasks of one half were run twice, by two builds of the tool that differ in a fix that does not touch them, and every stage, every per-instance outcome of every arm and every search cost came out identical.
